transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-01-22 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hale (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Amina Rahman (CTO - Cobalt), Luis Ortega (ML Eng - Cobalt), Sana Patel (Security - Cobalt), Tom Ellis (Product - Cobalt)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery on model selection and deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Key concerns: long context needs (up to 50k tokens), multilingual support, tool/function-calling, security (KMS, VPC), and benchmarking. Agreed next steps: pricing, security docs, benchmark run, PoC kickoff.

Topics: model families, context length and token cost, multilingual evaluation, function/tool calling, dedicated capacity & VPC, SOC2/KMS, quantization and latency tradeoffs.

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Jordan Hale: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll give it like a quick agenda - I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE, with Maya, our SE. Amina, Luis, thanks for your time.
00:08 Dr. Amina Rahman: Thanks Jordan, appreciate it. We're trying to pick models and deployment modes for our document understanding pipeline, plus some multi-lingual customer support stuff.
00:15 Jordan Hale: Great, can you describe current stack and constraints real quick?
00:20 Luis Ortega: Yeah so currently we run a mix - some on-prem inference for PII workloads and some cloud models for customer-facing features. Main pain points: context length - we have documents that require 30k to 50k token windows; also need function calling to integrate with internal tools, and multi-language support (EN, FR, DE, JA). Latency needs are moderate, 200-500ms for most calls but spikes okay for batch jobs.
00:40 Maya Chen: When you say function calling, is that structured tool calls or more like external API calls?
00:45 Luis Ortega: Mostly structured tool calls - extracting entities and then calling internal microservices. Also some plugin-like calls to fetch account state.
00:52 Sana Patel: From security side, we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), audit logs, and customer-managed keys (KMS). For some datasets, we need VPC/private deployment or on-prem option.
01:05 Jordan Hale: That's consistent with other enterprise asks. Quick callout: Redwood supports hosted API, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private deployments with VPC/on-prem. The same API surface across modes. For 50k token context we have model choices and some optimized kernels - Maya can go into that.
01:20 Maya Chen: Yep - for long context there are two levers: model family and chunking/caching. Open models we often recommend that have long-context variants - some 70k/100k variants - but there's tradeoffs in latency and cost. Also quantization affects memory/latency. For your 50k windows we can test a 70k variant vs a sharded approach using prefix caching. Our runtime supports KV cache and prefix reuse which helps a lot for chat-style flows.
01:50 Dr. Amina Rahman: How accurate is multilingual performance across open models? We can't always use closed APIs for residency reasons.
01:57 Maya Chen: Multilingual varies - some open checkpoints have very good en-fr-de but drop on ja/kr. We usually recommend evaluating on your in-house prompt set; we can run an eval on Redwood's hosted catalog as a quick comparison. Also we have Redwood-verified performance profiles for some open models which show token throughput and regression notes.
02:15 Tom Ellis: Do you do function-calling like OpenAI's tools spec? We have downstream orchestrations that expect strict JSON outputs.
02:22 Jordan Hale: Yes, we support function/tool calling and structured outputs. We also have streaming responses and can include schema validation hooks in the runtime; SE can talk details.
02:30 Maya Chen: Implementation detail - we support tool-calling patterns and can enforce structured outputs; if you need strict schema we can add a post-parse validation step and roll failure cases into the fallback model.
02:40 Luis Ortega: Good. On hosted vs dedicated - what's the rough latency/cost delta?
02:46 Maya Chen: Hosted is fastest to get started and has pay-as-you-go pricing, but for sustained high throughput and predictable latency dedicated reserved pools are more cost-effective. We can give a delta once we know throughput. Example: for a 2k token avg call dedicated can be 30-50% cheaper at volume. For 50k context workloads it's more nuanced - memory and quantization matter.
03:05 Sana Patel: For data residency and KMS we probably need private with customer-managed keys. Is Private an on-prem install or VPC-hosted?
03:12 Jordan Hale: Both options - Private can be VPC with customer KMS/HSM integration, and we also have an on-prem package for air-gapped regs. We'll share the security pack.
03:20 Dr. Amina Rahman: Real world question - we tried an open model that claims 65k context but performance was poor and cost spiked. How does Redwood mitigate that?
03:30 Maya Chen: A few things - kernel selection and compilation in the runtime optimizes memory access patterns. Also you can use a hybrid approach: a long-context model for retrieval/condensed context plus a smaller model for generation, or caching repeated prefixes. We can also suggest a quantization profile matched to your accuracy needs.
03:47 Luis Ortega: What's the impact of quantization on multilingual accuracy?
03:50 Maya Chen: It can slightly degrade some languages, especially low-resource tokenization patterns. We recommend A/B tests; our Optimize toolkit can suggest quantization profiles per model and workload.
04:05 Tom Ellis: Are there any vendor lock-in concerns with model variants or SDKs?
04:08 Jordan Hale: Our API is consistent; you can pin model versions and rollouts. For private deploys you keep control of the model artifacts. We support standard weights formats for common open checkpoints.
04:20 Dr. Amina Rahman: Can we run a benchmark with our 50k token docs and multilingual prompts? We'd like hosted comparison first, then dedicated.
04:27 Jordan Hale: Absolutely. Maya will run the benchmark. We'll need a representative sample and expected QPS.
04:30 Maya Chen: Request: please share 200-500 sample prompts per language and a 24-48h expected throughput profile. We'll run both hosted and dedicated simulations and return metrics (latency percentiles, token cost, failure cases).
04:45 Luis Ortega: We can provide that by Monday. Also, any guidance on embedding/retrieval for long docs?
04:50 Maya Chen: For docs with 50k context we typically do chunk+embedding + reranker and then use retrieved chunks as condensed context. We also have a rerank endpoint. If you plan to keep entire doc in context, model memory and cost will be high.
05:05 Sana Patel: Regarding SSO and audit logs - do you support IdP provisioning and fine-grained RBAC?
05:10 Jordan Hale: Yes, SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC roles, and audit logs are all part of our enterprise packages. Private deployments can also forward audit logs to your SIEM.
05:22 Tom Ellis: How about SLA and uptime for Dedicated?
05:26 Jordan Hale: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. We'll include the SLA details in the pricing pack.
05:33 Dr. Amina Rahman: Any known compatibility issues with our stack - we're mostly AWS, EKS, and a subset of on-prem for regulated records.
05:40 Maya Chen: That's common; we support VPC peering and hybrid networking. For on-prem we'll coordinate networking and data sync patterns. For EKS we can run private controllers or pass through client connections.
05:52 Luis Ortega: A side question - do you have pre-built multilingual NER models or do we fine-tune?
05:56 Maya Chen: We have evaluation harness and can fine-tune on your labels. For many customers we recommend prompt engineering plus a small domain-tune if needed. Fine-tuning on open checkpoints is possible in Private.
06:08 Jordan Hale: Ok to recap next steps - Jordan will send pricing + SLA options, Maya will send benchmark plan and request sample prompts, and Redwood security will share SOC2/KMS/SSO docs. Cobalt to share sample prompts and regulatory constraints.
06:20 Dr. Amina Rahman: Sounds good. Any blockers on our side?
06:23 Sana Patel: None now but we'll review security docs.
06:25 Jordan Hale: Great - we'll aim to have the benchmark plan and pricing in 24-48h. Can we tentatively schedule PoC kickoff on Jan 26?
06:32 Dr. Amina Rahman: Jan 26 works for us.
06:35 Jordan Hale: Perfect - thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with links to the security pack and benchmark tracker.
06:40 Tom Ellis: Thanks, bye.
06:42 End of call.
